claims.text: Robust superconducting behavior in bcc HEAs is governed by the stability of the disordered bcc lattice.
A stable bcc lattice preserves the electronic structure and electron–phonon pairing interactions under extreme lattice compression.
Chemical-disorder averaging and minimal short-range-order effects are responsible for preserving the electronic structure and pairing interactions.
(TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 is a superconducting HEA with a bcc structure at ambient pressure.
The proposed intervention progressively raises hydrostatic pressure from ambient pressure to approximately 190 GPa while measuring low-temperature resistivity.
The pressure experiment should be conducted under well-controlled hydrostatic conditions.
Elemental bcc superconductors such as Nb and Ta provide a baseline for comparing Tc-versus-pressure behavior.
The bcc lattice of the HEA remains invariant under high pressure.
Chemical disorder blurs local variations in the HEA.
Chemical disorder maintains a consistent electronic density of states under pressure.
The combination of bcc-lattice stability and extensive chemical disorder prevents pressure from markedly disrupting electron–phonon coupling.
The combination of bcc-lattice stability and extensive chemical disorder prevents pressure from markedly disrupting the density of states relevant to superconductivity.
If the hypothesis is correct, the HEA Tc will continuously increase or remain robust at extreme pressures.
The HEA has a Tc-versus-pressure trend distinct from those of elemental Nb and Ta.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to HEA superconductors that are predominantly bcc and significantly chemically disordered.
Applicability of the mechanism to layered or non-bcc HEAs is uncertain.
The quantitative effects of individual element ratios and residual short-range order on Tc are not fully determined.
A reduced-disorder or partially ordered variant showing the same robust Tc pressure dependence as the standard disordered HEA would falsify the proposed role of disorder.
Failure of the standard HEA to show a Tc pressure dependence distinct from elemental bcc superconductors would falsify the hypothesis.
